decisions.issues: Clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and the chapter 3 row: bare-headed, wet long curly hair, thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin with only light stubble, small gold ear stud, the hinged iron collar with its side ring, and the torn ochre tunic. Rain runs over his face and a riveted wet bulwark sits behind him, so the setting matches the deck. The memory seeps in from the left edge as a dust stain, with no clean frame. Anonymous turbaned riders gallop away with their backs to us, and a fallen comrade lies face-down beside his dead horse. There is no blood and no text (the flags are plain), and Nagoji is not among the riders. Lettering: caption 0 fits in the low-detail cloudy sky at top left (x 0.02 to 0.48, y 0.02 to 0.20), clear of the flag. Caption 1 fits in the dust and rain-stain band at bottom left (x 0.02 to 0.45, y 0.80 to 0.98), below the fallen man's hand. Both captions stay well clear of his face. There is only one candidate, so there is no backup.

v12 was the only candidate. Nagoji himself is correct: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, empty hinged collar with ring, bandaged hands, wrist chain, hobble chain, bare feet, gripping a line at the starboard rail with a rope coil at his feet, and nobody looking at him. The crew beat also works (pumps, a knife in the teeth, a snapped mainmast with torn canvas, lightning), and there is sky for the captions. Two things fail. (1) The ornate stern castle stands outboard of Nagoji's rail, in the open sea. Its decorated transom faces the viewer and waves break against its own hull and waterline. At print size it reads plainly as a second galleon lying alongside, not as this ship's own aft castle, which contradicts the story (a single ship, and nothing out there but a spar). (2) The transom has a gilt nameboard at about x 0.88-0.92, y 0.32-0.37 carrying letter-like glyphs (pseudo-text). A smaller point: two background crewmen, near x 0.49 and 0.54 at y 0.46, wear grey steel helmets, which read as guards or uniforms rather than sailors in caps or head cloths.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: Nagoji on the right foreground, thrown against the starboard rail, bandaged hands gripping a line, empty iron collar, wrist chain, hobble chain, coil of rope at his bare feet, face and hair as now. Keep the barefoot crew at the pumps and rigging on the left and centre, the knife-in-teeth sailor, the snapped mainmast leaning with torn canvas, the lightning and the rain, and the clear sky at top-left and top-right. Fix the ship: there is only ONE ship in this panel, and beyond the starboard rail there is nothing but open black sea and waves, with no other hull, stern, castle or vessel in the water. The carved stern castle belongs to this same ship. It rises above the deck at the far aft end, straight up from the deck the crew stand on, continuous with the deck, bulwark and rail that Nagoji holds, which run back into it. Show its forward bulkhead and railings as seen from the waist, not a decorated transom facing the viewer, and never its hull or waterline meeting the sea. Draw no nameboard, name plate, cartouche, banner or carved letters anywhere on the ship. Any carving is plain scrollwork or plain gilt moulding with no letter shapes. No metal helmets on anyone: the sailors wear knitted caps, head cloths or nothing on their heads.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The camera is low-angle and medium-wide, so the two men read larger than the script's 'small, from a distance'. This matches the previously picked v12. The small gold ear stud cannot be seen at this scale. The rest of the musket barrel is implied behind Nagoji's near arm. His far forearm is partly bare below the cuff, but no brand is drawn. Everything else passes: clean-shaven chin, curled moustache, iron collar, ochre tunic and cream dhoti, bandaged hands, the wrist chain swinging, and one hobble chain joining the ankle cuffs. The guard wears a morion and a buff jerkin, loses his grip, and his musket spins away to the right. The butt strikes his wrist with no injury shown. The hatch is open to lightning and rain, the narrow ladder is fixed, and the lantern-lit hold matches 6.2, 6.4 and 7.2. There is no painted text, no painted balloons and no blood. The dark ceiling beams at top left (about x 0 to 0.33, y 0 to 0.28) hold the long caption, and the dark beams at top right (about x 0.78 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.3) hold 'Bone cracked.'

v10 is the only candidate. It was an edit of v09, and it removed the vertical chain above their heads. Several things still fail. (1) The chain they haul is a huge anchor-gauge chain, not the light pen chain that runs collar to collar in 5.2 and 5.3. (2) It does not pass through either man's collar ring. Both collars are already empty, which breaks 5.5, where the chain runs out through those side rings. (3) The ring hanging on its last bolt, which the script calls for, is not shown anywhere. (4) Nagoji's LEFT wrist has no manacle: the bandaged forearm leads straight to a bare hand. All the iron sits on his right wrist, and no short wrist chain is visible, so he does not match the ch3 bible row. What is right: both faces match their sheets (Nagoji has the curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and gold stud; Keshavrao has short hair, a faint moustache, a grey-brown tunic and no stud). The pose, the hold interior, the lanterns, the absence of text or balloons, and the dark beams at top left and top centre that leave room for lettering are all good.
decisions.correction: Keep the low frontal camera, the ship's hold with its glass lanterns and dripping beams, both faces and expressions, Nagoji's gold ear stud and clean-shaven chin, and Keshavrao's short hair and grey-brown tunic. Keep their braced pulling poses in the water, and keep the dark beams across the top left and top centre clear, with no balloons, boxes or text. Fix the chain and irons as follows. The chain they haul is the ordinary PEN CHAIN from the previous panels. It is the same light gauge as their own wrist and ankle chains, never a heavy anchor chain. It runs through the side ring of each man's iron collar, and each man grips the length in front of him in both manacled fists, pulling it level and taut toward the camera. There is no upward pull on either neck. Past their fists, the chain rises at a slant to the upper RIGHT foreground corner. There the iron ring hangs half torn out of a cracked, splintered beam, held by a single remaining bolt. The ring must sit clear of the top-left and top-centre lettering space and never directly above either head, and no chain hangs vertically anywhere. Nagoji wears a separate iron manacle on BOTH wrists over the bandages, joined by a short chain about a forearm long. His bandaged left forearm stays covered and turned from camera. Keshavrao's hands stay thin and unbandaged, with a manacle on each wrist.
